title: Kitty Warrior
author: Drew M.
desc: Building a fierce, feminine figure using resourcefulness from my top secret home base/weaponry/intelligence agency.

ex.note: When you get to 20 reps with both legs, transition to one leg at a time. After this, we discuss weighting the exercise.
Plant your feet in the middle of two even objects that can provide hand support. Try to go unassisted on the way down, and use assistance from your hands to do more reps.
These will start as an AMRAP. After you reach 8, we will then transition to weighted push-ups.
Simply hold as long as possible three sets in a row. When you “fall,” try to do bursts of reps until you reach failure again.
Easiest variation of push-ups. Use these push-ups to get as many reps as possible.
Find a stable place to both hands about shoulder-width apart. Slide feet forward and lean back. Pull your chest to the sky. Be careful please, make sure you can grip it without falling.
If no dumbbells, grab either a bag you don’t care about, or another item you can grip (bag of rice for example. Hold with both hands, and perform hammer curl. Do your best to keep weight consistent.
Using the bag or weighted item used for Hammer Curls, stand and hold with both hands behind your head, and lift. Start light, you dont want to rotate your shoulders too far back with heavy weight.
Master your body weight for a long time before holding objects to increase weight. Use hand support to start if necessary. Balance will get better with time.
Balance is a bit tricky, so consider supporting yourself with your hands to lightly stabilize you. Hold items to add weight when you reach 20 reps body weight.
Keep track of a consistent item to hold in front of you. Perform the exercise, and increase weight when you hit 10 reps on any set.
Use this to get as many reps as possible to feed your weighted push-ups.
Tree branch, plank, anything. Try to find a place to hang. If too unstable, do more inverted rows.
